rubric.result: Every sentence of `### Desired end state` is in the sum of the eight commits. (1) 'A new module tree server/src/coverage/ reads the coverage of a clone from the artefacts already on disk ... in that order': `COVERAGE_CANDIDATES` in server/src/coverage/artifact-files.ts lists exactly the five paths in the stated order (coverage/coverage-summary.json istanbul, coverage/lcov.info lcov, lcov.info lcov, coverage/coverage.xml cobertura, coverage.xml cobertura) and `ArtifactFiles.readingOf` walks them, answering the first `measured` one. (2) 'the percentage of covered LINES, covered / total rounded to one decimal': `LineCount.percentage()` is `Math.round((this.covered / this.total) * 1000) / 10`, and the three readers project only line counters (istanbul total.lines, lcov LF/LH, cobertura lines-valid/lines-covered). (3) 'no artefact reads as no-artifact; an artefact that cannot be parsed reads as unreadable-artifact; neither is ever reported as 0 %': `CoverageReadings.of` folds `total === 0` into `noArtifact()`, `CoverageRanking.readingOf` turns `UnreadableArtifact` into `CoverageReadings.unreadableArtifact()`, and `CoveragePayload.entryOf` sends `percentage: null` for both non-measured states, never 0. (4) 'GET /api/coverage answers every clone of the root ordered by coverage descending, with the clones that have no percentage last, each entry carrying id, state, percentage, lines, source and measuredAt (the mtime of the artefact that was read)': the route is mounted in server/src/api/routes.ts (`router.get('/coverage', ...)`), `CoverageRanking.run()` reads every clone of `catalog.list()`, `CoverageOrder` ranks measured before both non-measured states and sorts the measured by percentage descending with ties by id compared by code unit, `CoverageEntryPayload` declares the six fields plus `state`, and `measuredAt` is `stats.mtime` of the candidate that was read (pinned by 'the measure date is the mtime of the artifact that was read'). (5) 'The parse of an artefact is cached per clone and per artefact mtime, with the Cache of server/src/api/routes.ts': the key is `[repoPath, candidate.path, String(stats.mtimeMs)].join('\u0000')` over a `Cache<CoverageReading>` built with `createCache` of that file. (6) 'The server keeps listening on 127.0.0.1 only, web/ keeps importing nothing from server/, and no payload carries an author name or email': server/src/index.ts is untouched by the whole slice, web/ declares its own `RepoCoverage` in web/src/api/types.ts and imports nothing from server/, and `CoverageEntryPayload` carries no identity field, asserted by 'GET /api/coverage carries no author name or email'. (7) 'A «Campeones» block in the dashboard draws the ranking with name, percentage, bar, source format and age of the measure; it highlights the clone selected in the header and it says so when a clone has no data, when no clone has data, and when the API fails': web/src/Champions.tsx draws `row.name`, `row.headline`, the bar at `row.barPercent`, `row.source` and `row.age`, marks the selected row with `aria-current` and the accent background, shows the per-row sentence 'Sin datos de cobertura' through `coverageHeadline`, `ChampionRows.emptyHeadline()` when no clone is measured, and a `role="alert"` paragraph on a failed load; App.tsx mounts it outside the `summary !== null` guard. (8) 'npm run build, npm test and npm run lint green from the root': the Global verification ran green before me. No promise is delivered by one task and undone by a later one.

Eight commits, read in order against the eight `**Objective:**` lines, agree with each other. The tree is strictly additive: task 1 declares the vocabulary and the port, task 2 consumes them in `CoverageOrder` and `CoverageRanking`, task 3 adds the three readers, task 4 wires them into `ArtifactFiles` through the `READERS` table, task 5 exposes the use case over the wire and wires it into `AppDeps`/`createDeps()`, tasks 6 to 8 consume that endpoint from web/. No later commit deletes or relaxes anything an earlier one established: the only `-` lines in the whole accumulated diff are the routes.ts docstring ('The four endpoints' becomes 'The endpoints ... Everything but /coverage'), the `createCatalog(...)` inline call in app.ts lifted to a `catalog` const so the same instance feeds `CoverageRanking`, the routes.test.ts `depsOverTheSameFiles` arrow widened for the same reason, one import line each in App.test.tsx, client.test.ts, client.ts and format.ts, and the App.test.tsx `stubApi` ternary extended with the `/api/coverage` branch — every one of them an extension of the thing it replaces, not a reversal. No scaffolding for an intermediate state survives: nothing built a temporary shape for a later task to retire. No problem is solved twice: the ordering rule lives only in `CoverageOrder`, the `total === 0` rule only in `CoverageReadings.of`, the Spanish copy only in web/src/format.ts, and the row decisions only in `ChampionRows`. The duplication of the payload shape between server/src/api/coverage-payload.ts and web/src/api/types.ts is not two tasks disagreeing: the closed decision 'web/ never imports from server/' and task 6's objective both put it there on purpose. The mid-run amendment of task 5's `**Files:**` line, which added server/src/app.test.ts and server/src/api/errors.test.ts, changed no decision: both files build their own `AppDeps` literal and needed the new required `coverage` field, and both commits give them that field and nothing else.

No yardstick: the `## Señal` section of the review package opens with '(sin señal declarada — el issue no trae la sección "## Señal de observabilidad"'. This slice's issue was groomed with no observability signal, so there is nothing declared to measure the accumulated diff against, and I do not invent one.
